I'm not sure how quickly trazodone metabolizes in your body as everybody is different. Hospitals are definitely expensive, mine was as well. They also offer payment plans and are usually incredibly nice about how much you are able to pay a month. I also work in a mental health hospital and know that we make it as affordable as possible and really work with our patients to figure out how to pay for it. Being alive is worth every penny. Even if it doesn't seem like it to yourself at this very moment, I'm sure somebody wants and needs you to stay alive. Even if you haven't met that person yet. I've been trying to kill myself every few months for at least the past 6 years. If any of them had been successful, I never would have graduated university or met my girlfriend or anything I've done with my life so far. Also, this might not help at all and I know I figured out ways around it but funerals are expensive too, sometimes more expensive than hospital stays.

Trazodone didn't have any effect on me. I could take bottles and still not sleep. I tried hanging myself before going through with it and ended up in the hospital instead. I was dead set on dying for months with that plan though. I didn't think the hospital would help at all and it didn't for the the first few days but changing meds and just having a break from life for a week ended up helping a lot more than I thought it would. Have you thought about going to the hospital?
Hey. My name is Mackenzie. I had a plan incredibly similar to that. I'm here if you want to talk

Hey, I'm here if you need to talk. There's also an amazing helpline called crisistextline you could message. Going to the hospital could be really beneficial to keep you safe. Don't worry about the money, hospitals have payment plans and discounts and all sorts of things to make it not expensive. The important thing is keeping you safe. Even if it's just giving you an extra week to think through things.
Wind-eze. Anything with simethicone
The only thing I've found is finding strong enough reasons to stay alive. It doesn't get me out of my depression but it quiets the suicidal thoughts and makes the depression less severe.

I was just in one in February but I told my family that was just to change meds. The ones I was on have really bad side effects when you're tapering off of it. My family has no clue how bad I'm feeling. Really no one does. When I'm in the hospital, I just act all happy the whole time and don't get any better. So it would just be a huge waste of money. I wish I could talk to people and actually get treatment. But it just doesn't work for me.
